newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bonds trade sideways, follow Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bonds trade sideways, follow Treasuries.

text.p: U.S. corporate high-grade bonds traded sideways on the heels of U.S. Treasuries that remained virtually unchanged at midday.
Traders cited little activity among both high grade and high yield corporate issues Monday.
"It's fairly quiet with not much going on," said one high yield dealer. "The morning was firm and it's quieting down now."
Among the most active issues in the high-grade market were Ohio Edison and Centerior Energy Corp.
The two companies announced Monday that they have signed a definitive agreement to merge in a tax-free, stock-for-stock transaction.
Dealers said they saw spreads of Centerior tighter by 15 to 50 basis points on the bid side, but with no offer seen as yet. Ohio was quoted 25 basis points wider on the offer from Friday's trade.
Traders said they expect a surge of new issuance this week following last Friday's rally in the Treasury market and with the benchmark 30-year bond trading with a yield below 7 percent.
"It looks like a lot of people, given the rally last week, are looking to come in and issue some paper," said one high grade trader.
On Monday, Bank of Boston priced $200 million in A3/BBB-plus rated 10-year subordinated notes to yield 65 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries.

Another $1.350 billion in a three-part debt offering is expected to come to market out of Nationsbank. The deal consists of $500 milion five-year debt, $500 million 10-year debt and $350 million of a 20-year issue, syndicate sources said.
In addition, $1.0 billion in global debt is expected to price out of Ford Motor Credit Corp, sources said.
Daimler Benz is also expected to price $500 million in 10-year debt via JP Morgan Securities, sources added.
At midday, in the high yield market, prices were quoted up by about 3/8 from Friday's close, traders said.
Among active issues in the grocery sector, Ralphs Grocery Co was up 3/8 from Friday at 99 bid, 99-1/2 offered. Bruno paper was trading up 1/4 at 102-1/2.
Among other issues, WestPoint 8-3/4 percent debt gained 1/8 to trade at par bid.
Transtexas paper traded up 1/2 at 105 bid.
And First Nationwide 10-5/8 percent debt gained 1/8 at 102-1/2.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. treasury bond was trading off 2/32 at 97-12/32 to yield 6.96 percent.
